To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) Davydov- Scott ODE models for exciton-phonons in α-helix proteins are well approximated by the third derivative NLS equation, (ii) the observed pulse dynamics is explained well by the Airy PODE, and (iii) the observed pulse shape is explained well by linearized analysis of a Davydov-Scot ODE model.

the phenomenon of coherent energetic pulses propagating along protein chains, such as α-helical protein, is explained well by a Davydov- Scott type ODE system model, with the observed behavior being explained well by a combination of a linearized analysis and the linear Airy PDE approximation.

the phenomenon of coherent energetic pulses in exciton–phonon molecular chains is well explained by the third derivative Schrödigner equation, that the Airy equation explains a good part of the observed behavior, and that other significant features are instead explained well using linearized analysis of a system of ODEs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the numerical study of a nonlinear system of ordinary differential equations (ODE) describing the propagation of excitons in an α-helix protein chain.
numerical studies of the Davydov model for the propagation of an energy pulse in a molecular chain of protein α-helices.
the numerical simulation of the Davydov- Scott model of exciton- phonon molecular chains.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for a variety of molecular systems, the Davydov- Scott model is a very useful model, but that it is not a model that can be replaced by a simpler model such as the nonlinear Schr¨odinger (NLS) or Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equations.

the Davydov- Scott model is a very good approximation to the α-helix protein, but not to a single amide bond, and that the linearized version of the model, which is the Airy PODE, is the best approximation to the behavior of the Davydov system for the case of initial excitation of one amide-I bond.
the Davydov- Scott model is a good approximation to the behavior of excitons in protein molecules, but that the NLS approximation is not a good approximation to it.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, while the Davydov model is a very good starting point for understanding the basic behavior of exciton-phonons in α-helix proteins, the NLS equation is not a good model for the propagation of coherent energetic pulses, and that a third derivative NLS equation, which can be viewed as a linearized version of the Davydov system, is a better model for the propagation.
the ODE model, with its highly accurate conservative time discretization, is a very useful and reliable tool for the study of exciton-phonons and their role in protein dynamics.

the numerical results here are in good agreement with the analytical results, and that the numerical methods used here are highly accurate and unconditionally stable for the Hamiltonian system studied.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, while the NLS equation is an excellent tool to use in many cases, it is important to keep in mind the limitations of such a model, especially when dealing with exciton-phonons in biological systems.

, in contrast to the common belief, the NLS equation does not provide a good approximation for Davydov- Scott systems with realistic initial data and parameter values.
